Paul J. McMurdie

bibl.title: Exact sequence variants should replace operational taxonomic units in marker-gene data analysis

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the unit of analysis in marker-gene sequencing - what a row of the feature table denotes - and whether it should be a cluster defined by a dissimilarity threshold or an exactly resolved sequence
span.quote: The analysis of marker-gene data customarily begins with the construction of molecular operational taxonomic units (OTUs): clusters of reads that differ by less than a fixed sequence dissimilarity threshold, most commonly 3% ( Westcott and Schloss, 2015 ; Kopylova et al. , 2016 ).

span.label: should amplicon sequence variants replace operational taxonomic units as the standard unit of marker-gene analysis and reporting
span.quote: For analysis to be reproducible the fundamental units must be reproducible, and de novo OTUs are not. For analysis to be comprehensive the fundamental units must be comprehensive, and closed-reference OTUs are not.

span.label: reframes the case for ASVs away from RESOLUTION - the advantage everyone had argued - and onto CONSISTENT LABELLING: an ASV names a DNA sequence that exists outside any data set, so it can be compared, merged and predicted from across studies, which neither kind of OTU can do at once
span.quote: However, unlike de novo OTUs, ASVs are consistent labels because ASVs represent a biological reality that exists outside of the data being analyzed: the DNA sequence of the assayed organism.

span.label: critique
span.quote: A consequence of this often unacknowledged dual mandate is that OTUs struggle to serve both purposes well; the connection between OTUs and species is largely unfounded ( Stackebrandt and Ebers, 2006 ), and the most common methods often output numbers of OTUs an order of magnitude higher than the number of strains present in mock communities ( Kopylova et al. , 2016 ).

span.label: the same construct serving two orthogonal purposes - translating taxonomy and absorbing sequencing error - and doing neither well
span.quote: Molecular OTUs serve two different and orthogonal purposes. The first purpose is to translate taxonomic concepts developed in other systems into the context of high-throughput marker-gene sequencing of microbial communities by the ostensible equation of OTUs defined at certain thresholds with particular taxonomic levels (for example, 3% ribosomal OTUs are ‘like species’). The second purpose is to reduce the impact of amplicon sequencing error on measures of diversity and community composition by grouping errors together with the error-free sequence ( Eren et al. , 2016 ).

span.label: conceptual analysis of three feature types against four practical requirements (computation, meta-analysis, replication, forward prediction) plus a demonstration run on the TARA Oceans 18S data
span.term: conceptual analysis of three feature types against four practical requirements (computation, meta-analysis, replication, forward prediction) plus a demonstration run on the TARA Oceans 18S data
span.quote: As a demonstration of reusability and computational tractability on large data sets, the DADA2 method for ASV inference was used to process the 18S rRNA gene amplicon data from the TARA Oceans project, which contains ~766 million reads ( De Vargas et al. , 2015 ), on a 2016 Macbook Pro.

span.label: **A de novo OTU is a property of its data set, not of the biology.** `de novo OTUs are EMERGENT FEATURES OF A DATA SET, with boundaries and membership that DEPEND ON THE DATA SET IN WHICH THEY ARE DEFINED`
span.quote: Many methods for constructing these clusters have been developed, but in all cases de novo OTUs are emergent features of a data set, with boundaries and membership that depend on the data set in which they are defined.

span.label: and the dependence is not an artefact of finite sampling - `THE DELINEATION OF DE NOVO OTUs DEPENDS ON THE RELATIVE ABUNDANCES OF THE SAMPLED COMMUNITY **EVEN IN THE LIMIT OF INFINITE SEQUENCING DEPTH AND ZERO ERRORS**`. Better data does not fix it
span.quote: This data set dependence is not just a practical concern: the delineation of de novo OTUs depends on the relative abundances of the sampled community even in the limit of infinite sequencing depth and zero errors.

span.label: so the consequence is flat: `de novo OTUs defined in two different data sets CANNOT BE COMPARED`
span.quote: As a result, de novo OTUs defined in two different data sets cannot be compared.

span.label: **A closed-reference OTU is a property of the database.** `each reference sequence in the database DEFINES AND LABELS an associated closed-reference OTU` - so two studies using the same database can be compared, and that is the property the paper names `CONSISTENT LABELING`
span.quote: If the same reference database is used, closed-reference OTU assignments from independently processed data sets can be validly compared, a property we refer to as consistent labeling.

span.label: but the price is everything the database does not contain: `biological variation that is not represented in the reference database is NECESSARILY LOST during assignment`
span.quote: However, biological variation that is not represented in the reference database is necessarily lost during assignment to closed-reference OTUs.

span.label: and the database is not a fixed point either - closed-reference OTUs `EVEN DEPEND ON THE ORDER OF THE REFERENCE SEQUENCES`, so `reference databases must remain static or closed-reference OTU tables must be regenerated` to stay comparable
span.quote: In order to maintain comparability over time, reference databases must remain static or closed-reference OTU tables must be regenerated whenever a new or upgraded reference database is adopted.

span.label: **An ASV is a property of the organism.** `ASVs REPRESENT A BIOLOGICAL REALITY THAT EXISTS OUTSIDE OF THE DATA BEING ANALYZED: THE DNA SEQUENCE OF THE ASSAYED ORGANISM` - which is why ASVs inferred in different studies can be compared without a shared database
span.quote: However, unlike de novo OTUs, ASVs are consistent labels because ASVs represent a biological reality that exists outside of the data being analyzed: the DNA sequence of the assayed organism.

span.label: the inference is still not read-by-read - `the smallest unit of data from which ASVs can be inferred is A SAMPLE`, because a sequence is distinguished from an error partly by being seen more than once
span.quote: As a result, ASV inference cannot be performed independently on each read—the smallest unit of data from which ASVs can be inferred is a sample.

span.label: **Without consistent labels a result cannot be tested.** `The absence of consistent labels makes REPLICATING OR FALSIFYING previous results problematic, EVEN IMPOSSIBLE` - an association with a de novo OTU can only be retested by first coarsening it to taxonomy or to a diversity metric
span.quote: The absence of consistent labels makes replicating or falsifying previous results problematic, even impossible. Consider a significant association reported between a particular de novo OTU and a condition of interest. This association cannot be tested in a new data set, because that de novo OTU only exists within the data set in which it was defined. Therefore, results from the analysis of de novo OTUs can only be tested indirectly, by mapping de novo OTUs onto consistent labels such as taxonomy or reducing community composition to summary measures such as a diversity metric, and then testing the results at that coarser level.

span.label: **THE DIAGNOSIS.** `Molecular OTUs serve TWO DIFFERENT AND ORTHOGONAL PURPOSES` - translating taxonomic concepts into sequencing, and absorbing amplicon error - and `A CONSEQUENCE OF THIS OFTEN UNACKNOWLEDGED DUAL MANDATE IS THAT OTUs STRUGGLE TO SERVE BOTH PURPOSES WELL`
span.quote: A consequence of this often unacknowledged dual mandate is that OTUs struggle to serve both purposes well; the connection between OTUs and species is largely unfounded ( Stackebrandt and Ebers, 2006 ), and the most common methods often output numbers of OTUs an order of magnitude higher than the number of strains present in mock communities ( Kopylova et al. , 2016 ).

span.label: and the taxonomic half is the one that fails: `THE CONNECTION BETWEEN OTUs AND SPECIES IS LARGELY UNFOUNDED`, with common methods outputting OTU counts **an order of magnitude higher** than the strains actually present in mock communities
span.quote: A consequence of this often unacknowledged dual mandate is that OTUs struggle to serve both purposes well; the connection between OTUs and species is largely unfounded ( Stackebrandt and Ebers, 2006 ), and the most common methods often output numbers of OTUs an order of magnitude higher than the number of strains present in mock communities ( Kopylova et al. , 2016 ).

span.label: **The replacement inherits a limit the paper states itself:** `The same genome can contain MULTIPLE ASVs if there are multiple copies of the targeted genetic locus` - one organism, several units
span.quote: The same genome can contain multiple ASVs if there are multiple copies of the targeted genetic locus.

span.label: and exact resolution does not buy biological coherence: `there is STILL NO GUARANTEE OF ECOLOGICAL COHERENCE OR EVEN MONOPHYLY among genomes with the same ribosomal sequence variant`
span.quote: For example, while necessarily better than the customary 3% ribosomal OTUs, there is still no guarantee of ecological coherence or even monophyly among genomes with the same ribosomal sequence variant ( Berry et al. , 2017 ).

span.label: **and the authors say the naming does not do the work** - `APPEALING TERMINOLOGY SUCH AS 'RESOLUTION OF EXACT SEQUENCE VARIANTS' DOES NOT ELIMINATE THE LIMITATIONS INHERENT TO REPRESENTING A COMPLEX BIOLOGICAL ORGANISM BY A SHORT GENETIC BARCODE.` A paper proposing a new unit, warning against being persuaded by its name
span.quote: Appealing terminology such as ‘resolution of exact sequence variants’ does not eliminate the limitations inherent to representing a complex biological organism by a short genetic barcode.

span.label: the promised merging is conditional: ASV tables `can only be simply merged if the underlying sequence data was derived from the SAME GENETIC LOCUS`, in practice the same primer set, or after trimming to the overlapping region
span.quote: ASV tables can only be simply merged if the underlying sequence data was derived from the same genetic locus. In practice, this means that only studies using the same primer set can be simply merged, although ASVs from different-but-overlapping primer sets can be merged if the ASVs are first trimmed to the overlapping gene region.

span.label: **This is a Perspective, and the case is argued rather than measured.** The only quantitative demonstration is a tractability run - TARA Oceans 18S, ~766 million reads, on a laptop - which shows ASV inference SCALES, not that ASVs recover communities better than OTUs do. The accuracy claims are carried by citation
span.quote: As a demonstration of reusability and computational tractability on large data sets, the DADA2 method for ASV inference was used to process the 18S rRNA gene amplicon data from the TARA Oceans project, which contains ~766 million reads ( De Vargas et al. , 2015 ), on a 2016 Macbook Pro.

span.label: measuring OTU output against MOCK COMMUNITIES - samples whose true strain composition is known by construction
span.note: eliminates: the circularity of judging a clustering method by the clusters it produces; with a known answer, an order-of-magnitude excess of OTUs is a fact about the method rather than a discovery about the community · outcome: failed
span.quote: A consequence of this often unacknowledged dual mandate is that OTUs struggle to serve both purposes well; the connection between OTUs and species is largely unfounded ( Stackebrandt and Ebers, 2006 ), and the most common methods often output numbers of OTUs an order of magnitude higher than the number of strains present in mock communities ( Kopylova et al. , 2016 ).

span.label: asking what de novo OTUs do in the limit of INFINITE SEQUENCING DEPTH AND ZERO ERRORS - a thought-experiment control that removes sampling and error entirely
span.note: eliminates: the reading that data-set dependence is a practical nuisance that better sequencing would cure; the delineation still depends on relative abundances · outcome: held
span.quote: This data set dependence is not just a practical concern: the delineation of de novo OTUs depends on the relative abundances of the sampled community even in the limit of infinite sequencing depth and zero errors.

span.label: running ASV inference on TARA Oceans - ~766 million 18S reads - on a 2016 MacBook Pro, and depositing the resulting tables
span.note: eliminates: the objection that per-sample inference cannot scale; the demonstration is chosen at the size where de novo OTU methods are said to become prohibitive · outcome: held
span.quote: As a demonstration of reusability and computational tractability on large data sets, the DADA2 method for ASV inference was used to process the 18S rRNA gene amplicon data from the TARA Oceans project, which contains ~766 million reads ( De Vargas et al. , 2015 ), on a 2016 Macbook Pro.

span.label: `amplicon sequence variant` - a biological sequence inferred prior to amplification and sequencing error, distinguished to a single nucleotide
span.quote: ASV methods infer the biological sequences in the sample prior to the introduction of amplification and sequencing errors, and distinguish sequence variants differing by as little as one nucleotide.
